cases.title: COPY, ROTATE Copy and SCALE Copy of pit P3 each make a real CE pit: a CE line says it was numbered as new and the copy comes with its own PIT LABEL
cases.plan_item: COPY of a pit (triage group M3; daily card D15); BUG-665
cases.reviewed_against: builder-filled: Opus review still needed. Compared by the builder on 25 Oct 2026 with BUG-665 in BUG_CARPARK.md (Grip-Ctrl copy, ROTATE Copy and SCALE Copy of a pit or pipe: expected "the copy gets the same clean-up a COPY gets: new pit number, own labels, own record") and daily card D15 (COPY: "1 pit copied and numbered as new", new pit number, one U). The Grip-Ctrl copy of BUG-665 is not driven. BUG-210, BUG-288, BUG-666 and BUG-671 (other COPY faults of group M3) are not claimed.
cases.expected: The plain COPY of pit P3 (the control) prints "1 pit copied and numbered as new." and adds one pit block (layer STORMWATER PIT) and one PIT LABEL block (layer STORMWATER PIT LABEL). ROTATE Copy by 90 degrees and SCALE Copy by 1.5 of the same pit must each give the same: a CE line saying one pit was copied and numbered as new, and one new PIT LABEL block beside the new pit block, so the copy has a number of its own and is not a twin of P3.
cases.why_not_unit: The copy clean-up runs when AutoCAD ends the native COPY, ROTATE or SCALE command on the live drawing.
not_automated: The new pit's NUMBER is not read (the PIT LABEL attribute is not exposed by the object read, and the Pit Schedule cells are not asserted): the case reads the CE line and the presence of the label block. The Grip-Ctrl copy of BUG-665 is not driven.
If the rotated or scaled copy gets its label a few seconds after the command, the 8 second wait here would show it; a later label would not be seen.

cases.title: With the Settings tick "Clean up grip Ctrl-drag, ROTATE Copy and SCALE Copy like COPY" switched ON, ROTATE Copy and SCALE Copy of pit P3 each make a real CE pit: a CE line says it was numbered as new and the copy comes with its own PIT LABEL
cases.plan_item: COPY of a pit (triage group M3; daily card D15); BUG-665 with the switch ON
cases.expected: With linking.cleanUpGripRotateScaleCopies true in CD_Settings.json when AutoCAD starts, the plain COPY of pit P3 prints "1 pit copied and numbered as new." and adds one pit block and one PIT LABEL block (as R34's control); ROTATE Copy by 90 degrees and SCALE Copy by 1.5 of the same pit must each give the same: a CE line saying one pit was copied and numbered as new, and one new PIT LABEL block beside the new pit block. The case also RECORDS (never judges) whether each copy gets a cover text ("CL ...") and what the PIT LABEL of each copy reads. Result of the first runs (b3v1, 25 Oct 2026, Civil 3.0.75, switch ON): the plain COPY and the SCALE Copy get a PIT LABEL, a cover text "CL 18.88" and the "numbered as new" line, but the ROTATE Copy about the pit's own centre gets the "numbered as new" line and a pit block and NO PIT LABEL and NO cover text, so this case FAILS on the rotate label check (tagged EXPECT-FAIL BUG-665). R34so shows whether a ROTATE Copy about a point elsewhere does better. If this ever passes in two sessions the ROTATE Copy / SCALE Copy half of BUG-665 works when the switch is on, and R34 (switch off) is its true red. The drawing file on disk is unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The copy clean-up runs when AutoCAD ends the native COPY, ROTATE or SCALE command on the live drawing, and the switch is read from the real settings file when AutoCAD starts.
not_automated: Grip Ctrl-drag copy (the other half of BUG-665) is not driven. Whether the new pit NUMBER differs from P3 is read from the PIT LABEL block in R34sn, not here.
The switch is set only for this case's AutoCAD session; Tim's file is restored by hash. Whether the office should switch the tick on is Tim's decision (Monday question 8).
